## Before starting

Use the course RStudio session on Biowulf (100 GB RAM, as in the slides). Run `scripts/0_setup.R` once in the R console before class to install the packages.

## Part 1: Cell Ranger

Run this in the RStudio **Terminal**, starting in the course folder. It writes a new `cellranger_run`; the supplied `cellranger_backup` stays available.

```{bash cellranger, eval=FALSE}
bash scripts/0_cellranger/1_cellranger.sh
```

Open `results/day1/cellranger_run/outs/web_summary.html` when the run finishes. While it runs, use `results/day1/cellranger_backup/outs/web_summary.html` and inspect the supplied `outs` folder. The mouse analyses below use the supplied matrices, independently of this human PBMC demo.

## Part 2: Cell Ranger outputs to clusters

Matching script: `scripts/01_qc.R`.

### Load packages and checkpoint

```{r qc_1}
# Part 2: import the five precomputed 10x filtered matrices and QC.
# Run: Rscript scripts/01_qc.R

library(Seurat)
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(qs2)

project_dir <- "."
data_dir <- file.path(project_dir, "data")
output_dir <- file.path(project_dir, "results/day1")
plot_dir <- file.path(project_dir, "plots/day1")
dir.create(output_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
dir.create(plot_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
```

### The simplest import

Read one filtered matrix, create a Seurat object, and inspect QC.

```{r qc_2}
####################
#the simplest load in possible
####################
test <- Seurat::Read10X(data.dir  = "./data/10x_mouse/filtered_feature_bc_matrix/")
test
obj_test <- CreateSeuratObject(test,assay = "RNA",project = "test_demo",min.cells = 3,min.features = 0)
obj_test
obj_test[["percent.mt"]] <- Seurat::PercentageFeatureSet(
  obj_test, pattern = "^mt-"
)
colnames(obj_test@meta.data)
VlnPlot(obj_test,features = c("nCount_RNA","nFeature_RNA","percent.mt"))
```

### Import the five samples

Use a sample table and loop to repeat the same steps.

```{r qc_3}
####################
#let's do a little more reproducibly
####################
# "Reference" means non-5xFAD source material, not a matched WT control.
samples <- tibble::tibble(
  sample_id = c("10x_mouse", "GSM8824189_S_1", "GSM8824190_S_2",
                "A1331_Idol-Camk2a-WT-5xFAD", "A2022_Idol-Camk2a-WT-5xFAD"),
  study = c("10x_mouse", "Kersey_2026", "Kersey_2026",
            "Karahan_2025", "Karahan_2025"),
  condition = c("reference", "reference", "reference", "5xFAD", "5xFAD"),
  archive = c(
    file.path(data_dir, "10x_mouse/5k_mouse_brain_CNIK_3pv3_filtered_feature_bc_matrix.tar.gz"),
    file.path(data_dir, "Kersey_2026/GSM8824189_S_1_filtered_feature_bc_matrix.tar.gz"),
    file.path(data_dir, "Kersey_2026/GSM8824190_S_2_filtered_feature_bc_matrix.tar.gz"),
    file.path(data_dir, "Karahan_2025/A1331_Idol-Camk2a-WT-5xFAD_filtered_feature_bc_matrix.tar.gz"),
    file.path(data_dir, "Karahan_2025/A2022_Idol-Camk2a-WT-5xFAD_filtered_feature_bc_matrix.tar.gz")
  )
)


seurat_samples <- vector("list", nrow(samples))
names(seurat_samples) <- samples$sample_id

for (i in seq_len(nrow(samples))) {
  sample_id <- samples$sample_id[i]
  unpack_dir <- file.path(data_dir, "unpacked", sample_id)
  dir.create(unpack_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

  utils::untar(samples$archive[i], exdir = unpack_dir)
  matrix_files <- list.files(unpack_dir, pattern = "^matrix[.]mtx([.]gz)?$",
                             recursive = TRUE, full.names = TRUE)
  counts <- Seurat::Read10X(data.dir = dirname(matrix_files))

  seurat_samples[[i]] <- Seurat::CreateSeuratObject(
    counts = counts, project = sample_id, min.cells = 3, min.features = 0
  )
  seurat_samples[[i]]$sample_id <- sample_id
  seurat_samples[[i]]$study <- samples$study[i]
  seurat_samples[[i]]$condition <- samples$condition[i]
  seurat_samples[[i]][["percent.mt"]] <- Seurat::PercentageFeatureSet(
    seurat_samples[[i]], pattern = "^mt-"
  )
  message(sample_id, ": ", ncol(seurat_samples[[i]]), " nuclei before QC")
}
```

### Inspect QC

Compare genes per nucleus across samples before filtering.

```{r qc_4}
raw_qc <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_along(seurat_samples), function(i) {
  seurat_samples[[i]]@meta.data |>
    dplyr::mutate(sample_id = samples$sample_id[i]) |>
    dplyr::select(sample_id, nCount_RNA, nFeature_RNA, percent.mt)
}))
# utils::write.csv(raw_qc, file.path(output_dir, "01_nucleus_qc_before_filter.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

qc_plot <- ggplot2::ggplot(raw_qc, ggplot2::aes(x = sample_id, y = nFeature_RNA)) +
  ggplot2::geom_violin(fill = "#81b7be", scale = "width") +
  ggplot2::coord_flip() +
  ggplot2::labs(x = NULL, y = "Genes per nucleus", title = "Inspect QC by sample") +
  ggplot2::theme_classic()
# grDevices::png(file.path(plot_dir, "01_genes_per_nucleus.png"),
#                width = 9, height = 5, units = "in", res = 160)
print(qc_plot)
# grDevices::dev.off()
```

### Filter and merge

Apply the teaching thresholds, count the remaining cells, and merge the samples.

```{r qc_5}
for (i in seq_along(seurat_samples)) {
  # Teaching thresholds; inspect sample-specific QC before keeping them.
  keep_cells <- colnames(seurat_samples[[i]])[
    seurat_samples[[i]]$nFeature_RNA >= 200 &
      seurat_samples[[i]]$percent.mt <= 5
  ]
  seurat_samples[[i]] <- base::subset(seurat_samples[[i]], cells = keep_cells)
}

cell_counts <- tibble::tibble(
  sample_id = samples$sample_id,
  study = samples$study,
  condition = samples$condition,
  n_cells_after_qc = vapply(seurat_samples, ncol, numeric(1))
)
# utils::write.csv(cell_counts, file.path(output_dir, "01_sample_summary.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
print(cell_counts)

obj <- base::merge(seurat_samples[[1]], y = seurat_samples[-1],
                   add.cell.ids = samples$sample_id, project = "BDMS_sc_2026")
DefaultAssay(obj) <- "RNA"
# Tip: qs2 is much quicker for saving/loading these objects: https://github.com/qsbase/qs2
qs_save(obj, file.path(output_dir, "01_merged.qs2"))

# Loading back in at the start of the next script:
# obj <- qs_read("results/day1/01_merged.qs2")
```

## Part 2: Integration and markers

Matching script: `scripts/02_integrate.R`. This reads `01_merged.qs2` and saves `02_integrated.qs2`.

### Load packages and checkpoint

```{r integration_1}
# Part 2: integrate study batches and inspect markers.

library(Seurat)
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(qs2)
library(patchwork)

project_dir <- "."
result_dir <- file.path(project_dir, "results/day1")
plot_dir <- file.path(project_dir, "plots/day1")
dir.create(plot_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

obj <- qs_read(file.path(result_dir, "01_merged.qs2"))
DefaultAssay(obj) <- "RNA"
```

### Before integration

Normalize, select variable features, scale, and run PCA and UMAP.

```{r integration_2}
# The import/merge may already have created one counts layer per sample.
obj[["RNA"]] <- SeuratObject::JoinLayers(obj[["RNA"]])#purposefully put together
obj[["RNA"]] <- split(obj[["RNA"]], f = obj$study) #or split back out
obj <- Seurat::NormalizeData(obj)
obj <- Seurat::FindVariableFeatures(obj, nfeatures = 2000)
obj <- Seurat::ScaleData(obj)
obj <- Seurat::RunPCA(obj, npcs = 30)
obj <- Seurat::RunUMAP(obj, reduction = "pca", dims = 1:20,
                       reduction.name = "umap.unintegrated")
#let's take a short look
DimPlot(obj,reduction = "umap.unintegrated",group.by = "study")
#what if we blew through this stop sign...
obj <- Seurat::FindNeighbors(obj, reduction = "pca", dims = 1:20)
obj <- Seurat::FindClusters(obj,resolution = 2)
DimPlot(obj,reduction = "umap.unintegrated",group.by = "seurat_clusters",label = T)+NoLegend()
```

### Harmony integration

Explicitly handle the sample and study batches.

```{r integration_3}
#so what would happen if we then explictly deal with the batches (studies)
obj[["RNA"]] <- JoinLayers(obj[["RNA"]])
obj <- NormalizeData(obj)
obj <- FindVariableFeatures(obj, nfeatures = 2000)
obj <- ScaleData(obj, vars.to.regress = c("percent.mt"))#regressing something like percent.mt will stop the percent.mt from driving clustering
obj <- RunPCA(obj)
library(harmony)
obj <- RunHarmony(object = obj, reduction = "pca", group.by.vars = c("orig.ident","study"),
                         reduction.save = 'harmony', plot_convergence = T, lambda = NULL)
print(ElbowPlot(obj, reduction = "harmony", ndims = 50))

n_dims <- 10
obj <- FindNeighbors(obj, reduction = "harmony", dims = 1:n_dims)
obj <- RunUMAP(obj, reduction = "harmony", dims = 1:n_dims, reduction.name = "umap_harmony")

DimPlot(obj,reduction = "umap_harmony",split.by = "study",group.by = "study")
```

### Compare resolutions

Compare cluster resolutions on the same integrated map.

```{r integration_4}
obj<-FindClusters(obj,resolution = c(0.1,0.5,1.0))


p1<-DimPlot(obj,reduction = "umap_harmony",group.by = "RNA_snn_res.0.1",label = T)+NoLegend()
p2<-DimPlot(obj,reduction = "umap_harmony",group.by = "RNA_snn_res.0.5",label = T)+NoLegend()
p3<-DimPlot(obj,reduction = "umap_harmony",group.by = "RNA_snn_res.1",label = T)+NoLegend()

p1|p2|p3


obj$RNA_snn_res.2<-NULL

library(clustree)

clustree(obj,prefix = "RNA_snn_res.")
```

### Inspect markers

Look at known markers and calculate markers for the active clustering.

```{r integration_5}
FeaturePlot(obj,features = c("Plp1","Aqp4","Map2"),reduction = "umap_harmony",ncol = 3)

Idents(obj)<-"RNA_snn_res.0.1"
DotPlot(obj,features = c("Plp1","Aqp4","Map2"))

Idents(obj) <- "RNA_snn_res.0.1"
markers <- Seurat::FindAllMarkers(#it will take whatever the Active idents are so need to run the line before to make sure it is the cluster you want!
  obj, assay = "RNA", only.pos = TRUE,
  min.pct = 0.2, logfc.threshold = 0.25)
#if you get a warning message about "immunogenomics/presto", please kill the command with the stop sign by the console below and run: remotes::install_github("immunogenomics/presto")
#then retry!
head(markers)
qs_save(obj,file = "./results/day1/02_integrated.qs2")
```

## Part 2.5: Begin annotation

Matching script: `scripts/03_saha_markers.R`. Begin here if time permits; otherwise start here on Day 2. The saved inputs and marker-based object let us resume in a fresh session.

### Load packages and checkpoint

```{r saha_markers_1}
# Part 2.5: begin SAHA annotation at resolution 0.1.
# Start here near the end of Day 1, or at the beginning of Day 2.

library(Seurat)
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(qs2)
library(SAHA)
library(SAHAdata)

obj <- qs_read(file = "./results/day1/02_integrated.qs2")
```

### Marker-based annotation

Begin at resolution 0.1 and compare cluster markers with the Allen reference.

```{r saha_markers_2}
Idents(obj) <- "RNA_snn_res.0.1"
saha_inputs<- Seurat2SAHA(obj)
qs_save(saha_inputs, file = "results/day2/annotation/03_inputs_res01.qs2")  

# Allen ISOCTX is an annotation aid. Review label validity for each tissue.
data("ISOCTX_Markers", package = "SAHAdata")
data("ABC_meta", package = "SAHAdata")
ann <- SAHA::Create_SAHA_object(
  query = saha_inputs$markers, db = ISOCTX_Markers, data_type = "Markers"
)
ann <- SAHA::Initialize_Markers(ann)
ann <- SAHA::Run_Marker_Based(ann)
ann <- SAHA::Create_MarkerBased_Viz(ann, meta = ABC_meta)
auto <- SAHA::AutoAnnotate(ann, data_type = "Markers")
print(auto)

print(ann@results$marker_based$dotplot_all)

# Stop here if we have reached the end of Day 1.
qs_save(ann, file = "results/day2/annotation/03_markers_res01.qs2")
```
